Education for Sustainable Development

Integrating Sustainability into Higher Education: Theories, Concepts, and Practical Strategies

A co-created course integrating sustainability into curricula. Designed as a modular, openly licensed resource for HEIs in the Global South and North.

What you will learn

Learning Outcomes

By the end of this course, students should be able to:

1

To empower higher education faculty in Kenya with the knowledge, tools, and strategies to effectively integrate sustainable development (SD) concepts and theories into their teaching.

2

To provide an in-depth understanding of key SD concepts and theories.

3

To guide participants in establishing thematic connections between SD and their respective fields.

4

To highlight the importance of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) for sustainable futures, and to provide knowledge, tools, and strategies to integrate ESD approaches into their teaching.

5

To develop an individual action plan on how to integrate SD and ESD approaches into teaching.

6

Communicate sustainability challenges to diverse audiences including policy makers and civil society.

Session overview

Course Sessions

The course runs over 5-6 weeks combining lectures, workshops, field sessions, and guest expert inputs. Each session page includes materials, tasks, and localisation notes for partner institutions.

Foundations ### Session 01: Introduction to Sustainable Development

Participants learn to define sustainable development and its core principles, identify key challenges that sustainability seeks to address.

View session

Foundations ### Session 02: Interlinkages of Sustainability Dimensions and Role of Science & Education

Participants examine the links between social, economic, and environmental dimensions of sustainable development.

View session

Foundations ### Session 03: Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) & Constructive Alignment

Participants gain an understanding of the principles and importance of ESD as well as of the concept of constructive alignment in designing effective courses.

View session

Presentations ### Session 04: Presentation of Action Plans

Participants present the action plan they have developed on how to integrate (E)SD into their own teaching. .

View session

Reflexions ### Session 05: Reflection session

Participants provide feedback on course content, structure, etc.

View session

Open Educational Resource

Adapt This Course

This course is designed to be adopted and adapted by Higher Education Institutions worldwide. Materials are modular — individual sessions can be integrated without running the full course. Each session includes a recommendations for facilitation.
